findings.message: This change modifies plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (image/entrypoint.sh) and adds plugin tests, but the diff bumps no version. None of the plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json or .claude-plugin/marketplace.json plugins[] versions change. Bump every one of them to the same new version.
findings.scenario: Merge this PR → the marketplace still advertises the specclaw-fleet version from main (0.9.3 after c57281f), so an installed client sees no update and keeps the old entrypoint with the unstripped AZDO_REPO derivation.

findings.message: The fix strips exactly one trailing '/' (`${FLEET_REPO_URL%/}`), so it covers only the named case `r/`. When the URL has more than one trailing slash, `.git` is never reached and `##*/` yields an empty name. A suffix in another case (`.GIT`) is also kept. Strip all trailing slashes, for example with a loop or `shopt -s extglob; ${url%%+(/)}`, then strip `.git` case-insensitively. Add `r//` and `r.git//` rows to the ac7 table.
findings.scenario: FLEET_REPO_URL=https://dev.azure.com/o/p/_git/r.git// → repo_name='…/r.git/' → AZDO_REPO='' and the WARN is printed. The expected result is AZDO_REPO=r, so pr-azdo fails for a repo URL that git clones fine.

findings.message: When AZDO_REPO is empty, the pod only writes a WARN to stderr in the pod log and then runs the whole agent session anyway. The failure only shows up later, when pr-azdo fails. Consider surfacing it on the work item (tracker comment or field), or failing before the agent starts, so the operator sees why no PR was created.

The WARN rows only grep for the warning text. They do not assert what the agent actually saw: that $TMP/azdorepo is empty and not stale or a wrong derived value. Also assert the azdorepo content on WARN rows so that a regression that both warns and exports a bogus name is caught.

`2>/dev/null` on every site call still hides why a row failed. Exec errors, missing libs and SIGPIPE messages all collapse into an rc/got mismatch with no stderr, which is exactly how the earlier E2BIG went unnoticed. Capture stderr to a file and print it in the failure line.
